questions.q: How many lines of symmetry does a scalene triangle have?
questions.a: A scalene triangle has 0 lines of symmetry. A wrong answer (like saying 1 or 3) reveals the student does not understand that "scalene" means all sides are of different lengths, preventing any perfect fold.

questions.q: If you draw a line through a rectangle that is not a square, does it always create a line of symmetry?
questions.a: No, only lines passing through the midpoints of opposite sides are lines of symmetry; diagonals in a non-square rectangle do not create identical halves. This reveals a misunderstanding where students assume any line cutting a shape in half is a "line of symmetry."

questions.q: A square has 4 lines of symmetry. Using a paper square, explain where these lines are located.
questions.a: Two lines pass through the midpoints of opposite sides (horizontal and vertical), and two lines are the diagonals connecting opposite vertices. A wrong answer suggests the student hasn't visualized the folding process for the diagonals.

questions.q: Compare the lines of symmetry in an equilateral triangle and an isosceles triangle.
questions.a: An equilateral triangle has 3 lines of symmetry (one from each vertex), whereas an isosceles triangle has only 1 (from the vertex between the equal sides). Confusing these indicates a lack of connection between side length equality and symmetry.

questions.q: Can a shape have a line of symmetry if it is "tilted" or rotated?
questions.a: Yes, a line of symmetry is a property of the shape's own structure, regardless of its orientation in space. A wrong answer shows the student relies on visual orientation rather than the geometric properties of the shape.

questions.q: Draw a shape that has exactly two lines of symmetry, and explain why a third line cannot exist for your shape.
questions.a: A rectangle (that is not a square) is a classic example. A third line (like a diagonal) would result in parts that do not overlap, meaning the symmetry property is strictly bound by the rectangle's dimensions.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: A line of symmetry is an ______ line that divides a 2D shape into two identical mirror halves, such that if the shape were folded along this line, both parts would overlap perfectly.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you have a piece of paper cut in the shape of a heart; if you fold it down the middle, the left side lands ______ on the right.

Fill in the blank: A line of symmetry is an imaginary line that divides a ______D shape into two identical mirror halves, such that if the shape were folded along this line, both parts would overlap perfectly.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to identify, draw, and count the lines of symmetry for various polygons and simple 2D shapes by mentally or physically visualizing a fold.
